text:
maya: FYI — Acme reported a large gap between their invoice and our usage export. Invoice shows 31,984,512 embedding units for 2026-03-12..18 but /exports/usage/2026-03-18/acme-embeds.csv only has ~22M rows. Can billing engineering take a look?
jon: looking now. quick q — are we counting retried requests (rate-limit retries) as billable in ledger? that could explain some of it.
alex: we do mark retried attempts as billable if they completed successfully and produced tokens/embeds. short-circuit failures are not billable.
jon: initial diff by client_id shows ~9.8M units more on the invoice. I'm joining ledger_events to the s3 export to find missing requests.
jon: query snippet: SELECT e.request_id, e.client_id, e.units, e.status, s.s3_path FROM ledger_events e LEFT JOIN s3_exports s ON e.request_id = s.request_id WHERE e.client_id = 'acme-corp' AND e.event_time BETWEEN '2026-03-12' AND '2026-03-18' AND e.units > 0 AND s.request_id IS NULL;
chandra: Acme says they hit a burst yesterday and saw a bunch of 429s, then retried with linear backoff. They assume retries are deduped.
maya: customer-facing: determine whether dedupe happened, and whether to issue a credit or backfill CSV so their accounting lines up.
jon: raw results show ~9,820,001 requests marked 'completed' in ledger but no matching s3 export rows. Many have X-Retry-Count > 0.
alex: suggests our export job (embeds-export-v2) is dropping rows written via the streaming pipeline vs the batch sink. suspect a windowing/race bug under high concurrency.
jon: uploading a sample of missing request_ids to S3 for infra: s3://redwood-debug/finance/acme/missing-1799912345/sample-100.csv
ops-bot: Background job embed-export-v2 completed at 2026-03-19T02:12:14Z; duration 03:48:12; processed 120M rows; errors: 12
chandra: Can we re-run an export for that window without impacting current exports? We'll need a one-off backfill.
alex: yes. we'll create a backfill job that scans ledger_events for that client+window and emits the export format. will run on a dedicated worker pool.
jon: if missing rows are true completes we should backfill the CSV (preferred) or roll a negative adjustment if invoice already finalized. Acme's invoice is still pending.
maya: preference: backfill CSV and re-generate invoice items. avoid manual credits unless backfill fails.
jon: plan: (1) alex to spin backfill job id backfill-1799912345 writing to s3://billing-backfills/acme/2026-03-12_18/; (2) validations: checksum/count vs ledger; (3) re-run invoice generation dry-run and diff; (4) if resolved push final.
alex: backfill queued on dedicated pool. ETA ~45m. backfill script: python tools/backfill_exports.py --client acme-corp --from 2026-03-12 --to 2026-03-18 --out s3://billing-backfills/acme/2026-03-12_18/ --job-id backfill-1799912345
jon: validation sample after backfill should match ledger rows: aws s3 cp s3://billing-backfills/acme/2026-03-12_18/part-00000.csv - | cut -d, -f1 | sort | comm -23 - <(psql -At -c "select request_id from ledger_events where client_id='acme-corp' and event_time between '2026-03-12' and '2026-03-18'" | sort) | wc -l
ops-bot: backfill-1799912345 started at 2026-03-19T03:02:10Z on pool billing-backfills-dedicated
jon: quick check after 10m — head of the backfill output shows rows for many missing request_ids. matching looks promising.
chandra: once counts confirmed, I'll message Acme with timeline and that we prefer backfill->regenerate invoice.
maya: add finance audit note: reason = exports pipeline race led to retries written to ledger but dropped by the export job. tag for postmortem.
alex: root cause: exports pipeline acknowledged streaming writes before parquet materialization in some shards under very high concurrency. fix in PR #4321 strengthens flush/ack ordering and retries failed parquet writes.
jon: after full run, backfill produced 9,820,001 rows; ledger count for that client/window was 9,820,001; exports now reconciled. re-run invoice generator dry-run shows consistent totals; final invoice regenerated.
maya: chandra — please draft customer message: timeline, what we did, final invoice will be regenerated, offer CSV for records.
chandra: sent message to Acme; they asked whether rate-limit retries are billable going forward.
maya: policy: retries that lead to successful completions are billable. we should add a docs note and invoice help text explaining retry behavior.
alex: PR #4321 merged and canary deploy scheduled today. will link deploy id once live.
ops-bot: deploy deploy-2026-03-19-canary completed for env=canary at 2026-03-19T09:12:03Z
maya: closing loop: invoice regenerated and pushed; Acme confirmed CSV receipt and accepts final numbers. filing a short incident note to finance/incidents and tagging eng-interop.
jon: marking thread resolved. :white_check_mark:
